issues.description: Naming and interface mismatch: the problem statement and the template refer to an interface named 'Milkable' with method messageOnMilk(), but the solution introduces an interface named 'Dairy' (with messageOnMilk()) and leaves a Milkable.java file empty. This inconsistency (Milkable vs. Dairy, plus an empty Milkable.java) will confuse students about which interface to implement and may cause compilation or test failures because classes in the solution implement Dairy while the exercise and template expect Milkable.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the interface name across all artifacts. Either: (a) rename Dairy.java and its usages to Milkable (and ensure Milkable.java contains the interface in package de.tum.cit.ase with String messageOnMilk()), or (b) update the problem statement and template references from 'Milkable' to 'Dairy'. Also remove or populate the empty Milkable.java in the solution so that only the intended interface exists and all classes implement the same interface name.

issues.description: The problem statement and template expect an interface named 'Milkable' (students are asked to create/implement Milkable). The solution implementation instead introduces and uses an interface named 'Dairy' (e.g., Goat and Seal implement Dairy), while a Milkable.java file in the solution appears unused/empty. This name mismatch (Milkable vs. Dairy) refers to the same conceptual entity (the capability to be milked) and can confuse students when mapping the exercise requirements to the provided solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the solution's Dairy interface and its file to Milkable (and update all implementing classes to 'implements Milkable'), or alternatively align the problem/template to use 'Dairy' consistently. Remove or populate the unused Milkable.java in the solution to avoid further confusion.
